subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that skill's host run while dangerous host override names and cross-skill isolation remain enforced?
rationale: The documented host-run env behavior and user reports support delivery, but this is also the same credential boundary as open secret-leak work, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent semantics.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit keys explicitly listed under the active skill's config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, snapshot behavior, and cross-skill isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only allowlist
options.body: Require each skill to declare every sensitive env name in metadata and update docs or doctor diagnostics so users do not expect arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys to work.

options.title: Move to a different secret contract
options.body: Defer the env bypass and design a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit keys explicitly listed under the active skill's config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, snapshot behavior, and cross-skill isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history in the overlapping skill env, runtime snapshot, and SecretRef repair path.
